St. Paraskeva of Rome

Saints

St. Paraskeva of Rome

St. Paraskevi of Rome · St. Paraskeve the Virgin Martyr

Period
Second century;dates differ in the cited accounts
Region
Rome;places of preaching in the received life
Titles / vocation
Martyr · Virgin · Woman
Commemoration
July 26

Introduction

St. Paraskeva of Rome is remembered for preaching, steadfast confession and beheading. Her received life includes several imprisonments and miraculous deliverances before the final execution.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA names her parents Agathon and Politia. She studies Scripture, distributes her inheritance after their deaths and preaches among pagans. The account places her first arrest under Antoninus Pius.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Origins and first arrest

The Des Moines parish account describes a Greek Christian household in Rome, secular and scriptural education, and study of philosophy. It says her parents died when she was twenty and that part of her inheritance supported a women’s community where she taught before travelling. These details are the parish’s received narrative, rather than independently documented contemporary records.

[3] Published parish life · Origins,education and women’s community

Life and notable events

The received life recounts a red-hot helmet and immersion in boiling oil and pitch. The emperor is burned while looking into the cauldron; after she heals him, he releases her. In another city, the governor Asclepius exposes her to a serpent, which dies after she makes the Cross.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Tortures and deliverance

GOARCH explains Paraskeve as preparation and connects her Friday birth-name with the Gospel’s day of Preparation. The following Gospel passage supplies that explicit biblical vocabulary; it is Scripture about Christ’s burial, not a biography of this later martyr.

[4] Official calendar reading · Name and printed Scripture references

And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.

And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.

Canonical scriptural narrative in the identified historical English edition; later biographical traditions are separately attributed.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Mark 15:42–47

Death and martyrdom

Under a further governor, Tarasius, she is tortured and beheaded. The OCA gives140; the parish places the life approximately140–180. Those printed dates remain attributed and are not harmonized into an invented exact chronology.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Final execution

The parish likewise distinguishes final beheading from earlier deliverances. It recounts the destruction of idols in Apollo’s temple before the execution.

[3] Published parish life · Closing narrative

Writings and legacy

The OCA associates her tomb with healing accounts, including restoration of sight. These reported miracles belong to the ecclesiastical commemoration.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Closing paragraph

GOARCH commemorates her on July 26 and records her veneration in connection with eye ailments.

[4] Official calendar reading · Date and concluding sentence

Chronology

  1. Youth

    Studies Scripture.

    [1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Opening life

  2. Under Antoninus Pius

    Arrested for refusing idols.

    [1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · First arrest

  3. Final persecution

    Beheaded under Tarasius.

    [1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Execution
